description:
Minor works to listed building, interior decorations , bathroom refurbishment
Construction of single story timber clad summerhouse to rear of garden.
decision_conditions: <p>The proposed summerhouse, by virtue of its size, height, proximity to the boundary, and relationship to neighbouring habitable windows, would result in a harmful impact on the amenities of the adjoining occupiers of 6 Culford Mews through a loss of light and outlook and would result in an increased sense of enclosure to these occupiers, contrary to policy LP2 (Development and Amenity) of the Hackney Local Plan (2020), London Plan policy D6 (Housing quality and standards) and Hackney's Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD (2009).</p>

<p>The removal of several trees at the site without the prior written consent of the LPA, and the failure of the applicant to provide written evidence, such as a tree survey and arboriculture report, to justify their removal, fails to comply with policies LP46 (<span style="text-align: justify; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Protection and Enhancement of Green Infrastructure)</span><span style="text-align: justify;">, LP47 (B</span><span style="text-align: justify; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">iodiversity and Sites of Importance of Nature Conservation), </span><span style="text-align: justify;">and LP51 (</span><span style="text-align: justify; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Tree Management and Landscaping</span><span style="text-align: justify;">) of the Hackney Local Plan LP33 (2020) and policies G1 (Green infrastructure), G5 (Urban greening) G6 (</span><span style="text-align: justify; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline;">Biodiversity and Access to Nature)</span><span style="text-align: justify;">&nbsp;and G7 (Trees and woodlands) of the London Plan (2021).</span></p><p><span id="docs-internal-guid-43104ae0-7fff-a2f0-5985-98e34d592599"></span></p><p><span id="docs-internal-guid-6eb509cc-7fff-e69b-6252-7b24410e5686"></span></p>

<p>The proposed summerhouse, by reason of its excessive scale, footprint, and detailed design, would fail to appear as a subordinate or ancillary structure, resulting in the loss of over 50% of the historic garden curtilage. It would cause harm to the setting and significance of the Grade II listed building and would fail to preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the De Beauvoir Conservation Area, contrary to Section 16(2) and 66(1) of the Planning (Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, paragraphs 199–202 of the NPPF (2023), London Plan policies D1 (<span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; text-align: justify; vertical-align: baseline;">London’s Form, Character and Capacity for Growth)</span><span style="text-align: justify;">, D3 (</span><span style="font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; text-align: justify; vertical-align: baseline;">Optimising Site Capacity through the Design-led Approach</span><span style="text-align: justify;">), D4 (Delivering good design), and HC1 (Conservation heritage and growth), Hackney Local Plan policies LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character), LP3 (Designated Heritage Assets) and LP17 (Housing Design) and Hackney's Residential Extensions and Alterations SPD (2009).</span></p>
